title: JWT algorithm confusion RS256 to HS256
desc: Server accepted HS256 tokens signed with the public RSA key. Attacker re-signs token as admin.
steps:
1. Grab public key from /jwks.json
2. Change alg to HS256, role to admin
3. Re-sign with public key as HMAC secret
payload:
import jwt
token = jwt.encode({'role':'admin'}, open('pub.pem').read(), algorithm='HS256')

title: Password reset token never expires
desc: Reset tokens never expired. Old token intercepted via Referer could reset password later.
steps:
1. Request reset, capture token from Referer
2. Use token days later
3. Reset password — account takeover

title: OAuth state not validated — CSRF account takeover
desc: OAuth flow did not validate state parameter. Attacker forces victim to link attacker OAuth to victim account.
steps:
1. Start OAuth, capture callback URL
2. Drop state parameter
3. Trick victim into visiting attacker callback URL

title: 2FA bypass via response manipulation
desc: 2FA endpoint returned success:false. Changing to true in proxy bypassed 2FA entirely.
steps:
1. Enter wrong 2FA code, intercept response
2. Change false to true
3. Forward — 2FA bypassed

title: Account takeover via email change without verification
desc: Email change required no re-verification. Change to victim email then trigger forgot password.
steps:
1. Change account email to victim@target.com
2. No verification required
3. Trigger forgot password — reset goes to victim email

title: Auth bypass via SQL injection in login
desc: Login endpoint vulnerable to SQLi. OR 1=1 bypassed auth and logged in as first DB user.
steps:
1. Enter ' OR '1'='1'-- as username
2. Any password
3. Logged in as admin

title: Host header injection in password reset link
desc: Reset email used Host header to build URL. Injecting attacker domain leaked reset token.
steps:
1. POST /forgot-password with Host: attacker.com
2. Victim gets email with link to attacker.com
3. Victim clicks — token captured

title: OAuth token leakage via Referer header
desc: Access token in redirect URL leaked to third-party resources via Referer header.
steps:
1. Complete OAuth — token in URL fragment
2. Page loads third-party resources
3. Referer leaks token

title: SAML NameID manipulation — login as any user
desc: SAML signature verified but NameID not in signed portion. Modifying NameID allowed login as any user.
steps:
1. Capture SAML response
2. Decode base64, modify NameID to victim email
3. Re-encode and submit

title: Magic link 6-digit token brute force
desc: Magic link tokens were 6-digit numeric with no rate limiting. All 1M combinations brute-forceable.
steps:
1. Request magic link for victim email
2. Brute force 000000-999999
3. Valid token — logged in as victim

title: 2FA backup code brute force — no rate limit
desc: Backup code endpoint had no rate limiting. 8-digit codes brute-forceable.
steps:
1. Find backup code endpoint
2. Brute force 8-digit codes
3. Valid code — 2FA bypassed

title: Weak reset token — MD5 of username+timestamp
desc: Reset tokens were MD5(username+timestamp). Knowing username and time allowed computing valid tokens.
steps:
1. Enumerate valid username
2. Request reset, note timestamp
3. Compute MD5 for nearby timestamps
4. Use token to reset password
